body:
> This might be the same issue as https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/109734

Probably not, crash trace and error messages seems to be form editor inspector, not AccessKit, so it's likely a different issue.

> Probably not, crash trace and error messages seems to be form editor inspector, not AccessKit, so it's likely a different issue.

Yeah probably not. I thought it might be because video he sent in that issue is exactly what happens to me. It's definitely not an AccessKit issue for me though because I'm currently compiling with accesskit=no.

It looks like the issue is that the plugin used in the project claims to handle any object if the currently edited scene has a certain type of root node: [it doesn't use `p_object` at all](https://github.com/dementive/gsg/blob/main/src/gsg/tools/MapEditor.cpp#L504). This results in it claiming to handle both a mesh and the material on that mesh, and when you try to expand the material both the material and mesh fold states end up getting toggled in a way the inspector isn't expecting.

[The docs for `_handles`](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/4.4/classes/class_editorplugin.html#class-editorplugin-private-method-handles) note that 
> Each plugin should handle only one type of objects at a time. If a plugin handles more types of objects and they are edited at the same time, it will result in errors.

so this seems like an issue with the plugin rather than godot. 

I'm not sure if this type of crash is something we care about, I'll leave that for more experienced maintainers to decide. 

If we do care, the crash on [my simplified version](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21904181/clean_mrp.zip) starts happening from #108555 onwards, although it's moreso making an existing issue worse than causing a new issue, as the behavior is still partially broken but doesn't actively crash beforehand.

Thanks for looking into this that makes sense and I think I can get around it for now in my case by just excluding the Material class from my plugin. That will resolve the problem on my end then, I should be able to get around the crash now, so can close this issue if it was just my fault for misusing the API.

The reason I'm using `_handle` in such a weird way is because I need the plugin and all the docks it adds to be visible in a certain scene not just on specific nodes. Please correct me if I'm wrong and there is an easy way to do it but I looked for awhile and couldn't find any good way to do this without editing the Node3DEditor class directly. It seems like EditorPlugins just aren't designed for this kind of thing. So checking for the scene root in handle was my hack to make it work.

Still present in **4.7.1.stable**, reproducible 100% of the time on two platforms — macOS (Apple M4 Pro, Metal / Forward+) and Windows. That should rule out the device-specific suspicion raised in #116911.

**Steps (100% reproducible here):**

1. A scene with `StaticBody3D` → `MeshInstance3D`, whose `BoxMesh` sub-resource has its `material` set to a `ShaderMaterial` loaded from a `.tres`
2. Select the `MeshInstance3D`
3. Expand `Mesh` in the inspector
4. Click `Material` → the errors below are logged and the `Mesh` group collapses itself
5. Click the material thumbnail once more → editor dies

```
ERROR: Object '<Object#...>' was freed or unreferenced while a signal is being emitted from it.
ERROR: Cannot connect to 'property_list_changed': the provided callable is not valid: 'EditorInspector::_changed_callback'.
```

**The resource itself is fine.** Loading and rendering the exact same scene from the command line with `--script` (a real rendering run, shader compiled on Metal) works without a single warning, before and after the crash. The fault is in the inspector path, not in the data.

**Workaround:** move the material off the mesh resource and onto the node — `material_override` on the `MeshInstance3D` instead of `material` on the `BoxMesh`. That puts it at the top level of the inspector, so the nested `EditorPropertyResource` path is never walked. Both spellings are valid API with different semantics, but for a mesh used in a single place they are equivalent.
